title: Introduce temporal RBAC windows, KMS authorization gate, and audit-rollup pipeline
author: Maya Chen
description:
Motivation: Customers operating in multiple jurisdictions asked for stricter temporal controls on operator access (timeboxed RBAC), deterministic KMS routing for short-lived tenant keys, and compacted audit records suitable for long-term retention. This PR adds three coordinated pieces: (1) a temporal RBAC window evaluator (RBAC v2 extension) to support allow/deny rules with start/end times and timezone-aware evaluation, (2) a KMS authorization gate that asserts key residency and enforces a fallback to tenant-approved key providers when a region mismatch is detected, and (3) an audit-rollup pipeline that compacts per-request audit lines into hourly batches with provenance headers and integrity hashes for cheaper long-term storage. Changes are conservatively gated behind feature flags to avoid impacting current tenants.

What this includes (high level): - Temporal RBAC evaluator: new decision hook that accepts rule metadata (start_ts, end_ts, tz_hint) and integrates with the existing RBAC v2 decision cache. The hook supports clock-drift tolerance and a safe-fail deny-by-default mode. - KMS authorization gate: per-request middleware that checks tenant KMS affinity, verifies provider signatures on ephemeral keys, and routes requests to a fallback key provider when configured policy allows; exposes metrics for mismatches and fallbacks. - Audit-rollup pipeline: a new background worker that ingests raw audit stream (same format as existing writer), groups events by tenant/region/hour, computes a SHA256 provenance blob, and emits a compacted JSONL with rollup metadata. Rollups are signed using the cluster signing key and annotated with the KMS origin for forensic tracing.

Testing and rollout plan: - Unit and integration tests: added 26 unit tests for temporal evaluation, 8 integration tests exercising KMS fallback paths against the test-kms shim, and 6 end-to-end tests for rollup generation. - Canary: deploy feature flags off by default. Enable temporal RBAC for the internal security tenant and the compliance test workspace. Monitor rbaceval latency, decision cache hit/miss rates, and KMS mismatch metrics for 72 hours prior to broader rollout. - Migration: no DB schema changes; RBAC rules with temporal fields are ignored by older decision engines. Migrations will be executed via a safe data backfill job (separate PR) to annotate legacy rules with default windows where requested.

Backward compatibility: - Default behaviour when temporal fields are absent is unchanged. - KMS gate is opt-in via tenant policy; existing tenants continue to use current KMS selection. - Audit-rollup consumers can opt-in to receive rollups; raw audits remain available for 30 days before compaction in the canary policy.

Security considerations: - Fallback key providers are restricted by deny-list and requires tenant consent. - Temporal evaluation uses monotonic clocks for relative checks and wall-clock for absolute windows; system clock discrepancies trigger a deny-with-override audit path requiring operator approval. - Audit-rollups are signed to prevent tampering and include KMS-origin metadata for non-repudiation.

Checklist: - [x] Design doc: linear ENG-4821 - [x] Unit tests - [x] Integration tests with test-kms shim - [x] Feature flag gating - [x] Canary rollout plan - [x] Updated docs/rbac.md section (short note) - [ ] Backfill job (follow-up PR) - [x] Security review

Related: See ENG-4821 for design notes and SUP-1142 for customer incident that motivated this work.
